analogs.covers: Defence: the unbreakable ring or wall with a few bulls charging out
Life on the move: a huge nomadic migration guided by an experienced cow, bulls trailing behind

headline: A musk ox wall on a caribou-style migration, led by the eldest cow.

setting.label: Long migrations between feeding areas and nesting grounds
setting.note: Nomadic, migrating long distances in search of food. Males become territorial around food sources at the nesting grounds.

playsLike: You are a large, docile ceratopsian in an unlimited 'migration' guided by the eldest cow, with related males (a father and his sons) forming 'shields' at the rear. When a dangerous predator comes within 10 body lengths, an unlimited defensive formation closes, and up to 4 adults break out to charge. Grouped ceratopsians (Albertaceratops, Styracosaurus, Psittacosaurus) are protected inside the formation. Your eyesight is poor but your memory is long, so a remembered powerful predator may trigger a stampede instead.

why.text: An unlimited defensive formation where individuals step forward only one body length to strike. That is the musk ox ring (official inspiration).
Up to 4 adults, usually males, break the formation to charge the predator, as musk ox bulls do.
Led by the eldest cow with the most allies, 'in the constant hunt for food'. Caribou migrations are guided by experienced cows.
Male 'shields' follow at the rear and paw the ground to hurry stragglers along.
Large tier, 4,500 combat weight, 800 HP, sprint 900 held for 100 s.

notLike: Musk oxen live in small herds; Pachyrhinosaurus migrations are unlimited and mixed with other ceratopsians.
Caribou flee rather than form walls.
